mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as lower rates compress discount rates and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods with a 0.5% decline in FEDFUNDS over 3 months are not significantly higher than baseline (p>0.05) or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days are negative due to tightening monetary policy.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.5% are not significantly lower than baseline (p>0.05) or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) predicts returns: when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls, negative 20-day returns follow due to policy tightening amid disinflation.
failure_condition: 20-day returns in periods with FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL falling are not significantly lower than baseline (p>0.05) or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% year-over-year), a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past 3 months predicts positive 60-day returns as labor market tightness supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL>3.5% yoy) with UNRATE decline over 3 months are not significantly higher than baseline (p>0.05) or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 3 months predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as stronger housing activity signals robust consumer demand and economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods with a 0.5% increase in HOUST over 3 months are not significantly higher than baseline (p>0.05) or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days are positive due to a tightening labor market supporting corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in periods with UNRATE < 3.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (p>0.05) or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) predicts returns: when INDPRO rises and CPIAUCSL falls, negative 60-day returns follow due to supply chain improvements reducing inflationary pressures and prompting monetary policy easing.
failure_condition: 60-day returns in periods with INDPRO rising and CPIAUCSL falling are not significantly lower than baseline (p>0.05) or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), a 0.5% rise in employees (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months predicts positive 20-day returns as a strong labor market supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods with UNRATE < 4.0% and a 0.5% rise in PAYEMS over 3 months are not significantly higher than baseline (p>0.05) or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window < 0.03.
